Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥.

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

Industry observers note that “It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

Sources indicate that “I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the latest challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”.

It has been revealed that sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 23:38, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 02:10.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted he has "no idea" about whether he will be at Anfield beyond the end of the season.

Van Dijk has established himself as a Liverpool icon in his 389 appearances since joining the club from Southampton in 2018.

The Dutchman has helped the Merseyside club win numerous pieces of silverware, including two Premier League titles and the 2018-19 Champions League.

However, it is unclear how much longer he will play a part in Liverpool's quest for trophies, with his current contract set to expire at the end of the campaign.

Van Dijk recently commented on his situation while on international duty, insisting that he is "not in any panic" over his Anfield future.

The centre-back has reiterated his relaxed outlook in an interview with Sky Sports, in which he conceded he has "no idea" whether he will sign a latest Liverpool deal.

"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk stated.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

"At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game.

"Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the newly introduced year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a major part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

In a recent development, "If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer.".

At the age of 35, Van Dijk remains an integral part of the Liverpool squad, demonstrated by the fact he has played every minute of the club's 10 Premier League matches this term.

Van Dijk is now preparing to make his 350th Premier League appearance in Sunday's highly anticipated clash against rivals Manchester United.

The Netherlands international has made 282 of his 349 top-flight appearances in a Liverpool shirt after featuring in 67 Premier League matches for Southampton.

Van Dijk will hope to mark his milestone outing with a victory, although he has had to settle for seven wins in his previous 18 Premier League matches against Man United (D5, L6).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Recent findings suggest that hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso mentioned: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he stated.

Sources indicate that “But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

Sources indicate that “It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso stated: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very vital part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

In a recent development, this is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

In a recent development, hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury swiftly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

Sources indicate that none of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also revealed quality and a threat. The joke is right now on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

In a recent development, it is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a fresh reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I stated to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

According to recent reports, “Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. It has been revealed that heading into January, Milan need reinforcements and especially at the back. Matteo Gabbia and Fikayo Tomori’s injuries have depleted the depth, which has led to Sankhoun Diawara being a starter perhaps a bit earlier than planned.

Earlier this week, Record in Portugal stated that Sporting are willing to part with Inacio in the winter window but only for the right price, which could be north of €40m. Still, it marks a step forward from the summer, when a late attempt failed.

In a video on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano gave an patch on Milan’s pursuit of a new central defender and he confirmed that Inacio seems to be the man in pole position.

It has been revealed that “Let’s keep Gonçalo Inacio’s name there. Confirmation has also come from Portugal about what we’ve been telling you, that Inacio could be a key player in the January transfer window,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m reiterating what I’ve been telling you for months, actually, about the relationships, because agent Miguel Pino is the same as Ruben Amorim’s agent. They’re all Portuguese, Amorim coached Inacio at Sporting. Arriving in January isn’t easy, though: it means being ready to be thrown into the fire.

“It’s not always easy. Signing Gonçalo Inacio would mean Amorim signing a player he knows, with whom he speaks the same language, not just verbally but also on the pitch. There’s a different feeling, he wouldn’t have to explain anything to the boy.

In a recent development, “Milan are keeping in touch with the player, his departure in January is possible, the doors are open if necessary. Then we need to understand the conditions, the prices, it’s clear that Sporting isn’t just interested in giving away a player like that for any price.

“They’ll have to negotiate, and last summer, Milan – amidst the ups and downs of this negotiation – at a certain point hoped to be able to secure a deal that could include a very expensive loan with an option to buy, to make everything easier from a financial standpoint. Milan have several names on the list, but Inacio’s is definitely one to consider.”.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti will take charge of his 600th Serie A match as a manager against Venezia, and he is approaching it the same way he did his first.

Spalletti will become the sixth manager to reach this milestone in the competition's history, after Carlo Mazzone (792), Nereo Rocco (747), Giovanni Trapattoni (689), Gian Piero Gasperini (648) and Nils Liedholm (635).

Juventus have had a topsy-turvy season so far, but are unbeaten in their last two league matches, twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 with Fiorentina following a 2-0 win over Napoli.

And Spalletti will be keen to mark his landmark match with a victory.

"I am preparing with the same emotion as I did for my first in Serie A," he said about his landmark match.

"There were moments during this journey that marked my career as a coach. I'm very happy to have had this tour in football, because it was my life and what I always wished for.

"I learned to be happy even when things are not going in my favour, and I hope to keep going for as long as possible.".

Juventus sit seventh in the league with just 18 points after 11 games, with suggestions they could miss out on Champions League qualification for the second season running, but Spalletti is not yet worried.

"I do think we have that possibility, but our objective is to become something," Spalletti said when asked about their start to the season.

Recent findings suggest that "If we do that, then we can get good results and a strong position in the table. We have to rely on our work; we want to create habits for constant improvement.".

It is fitting that Spalletti's landmark match is against Venezia, whom he coached at the start of his career, though he was sacked twice in the space of one season in 1999.

Sunday's visitors to the Allianz Stadium sit 19th, with only six points so far, and they have lost each of their last six Serie A away games, but Spalletti had high praise for the team.

"I have fond memories of a melancholic but splendid city," Spalletti added of his time at Venezia. "Those were my first seasons. I had strong Presidential and directorial figures; the team was struggling, so I was fired and brought back.

It has been revealed that "I want to congratulate Davide Nicola, as wherever he goes in his career, he brings a solution to problems and fuels enthusiasm. They'll try to strangle us and then send strong strikers on the attack like Akor Adams, so balance is essential.".

After an assist against Fiorentina and a goal and an assist against AZ, Randal Kolo Muani could be involved in a goal in three consecutive club appearances in all competitions for the first time since between May and June 2025.

That was also for Juventus when he got a goal against Venezia in Serie A, a brace against Al Ain and an assist against Wydad Casablanca in the Club World Cup.

Since Serie A returned to a 20-team format in 2004-05, Antoine Hainaut (four – two goals, two assists) is the first Venezia defender to have a goal involvement in more than three goals in a single top-flight season.

He set up Toma Basic's opener against Udinese before the international break, but also led that game in shots (four) and touches in the opposition box (six), alongside his two chances created.

Juventus are unbeaten in their last 14 Serie A matches against Venezia (W11 D3), with the Winged Lions' last victory against the Bianconeri dating back to April 1962 (3-0 at the Penzo).

In fact, Juventus have never lost in 14 home Serie A games against Venezia (W11 D3).

Among the teams presently in the top-flight, Venezia are one of only two sides against whom Juventus have always remained unbeaten in home league matches, along with Frosinone (W2 D1).

Following their recent success against Udinese, Venezia could win two consecutive Serie A matches for the first time since November 2021 (against Roma and Bologna on that occasion).

But Juventus have picked up 22 points from a possible 24 in their last eight Serie A matches against newly promoted sides (W7 D1), scoring 21 goals in the process, and conceding just one goal in their most recent six games against such teams.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 04:57.

Werder Bremen will be battling to keep their unlikely European dream alive on Sunday, when they welcome Hamburger SV to the Weserstadion for a Bundesliga Nordderby.

Die Werderaner are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while HSV are keen to pick up where they left off prior to the international break.

Daniel Thioune guided Werder to safety last term after taking the helm in early February, though his sights are set much higher this time around with his team sat in a strong position upon the league's return.

Nine matches into the campaign, Die Werderaner are sixth in the Bundesliga table, where their tally of 15 points has them two clear of seventh-placed Elversberg and just three shy of RB Leipzig in fourth.

Securing European football of any variety would be a major accomplishment for Thioune, who is at the moment in his first top-flight role as manager, not to mention that the club last appeared on the continental stage back in the 2010-11 Champions League group stage.

However, Werder signed off for the international break with a 1-0 defeat at Stuttgart on November 7, their second loss in three matches after a 3-2 beating by Borussia Dortmund in the DFB-Pokal in late October.

In fairness to the Green-Whites, they fought back from 2-0 down against BVB thanks to a brace from Niclas Fullkrug, only to lose out to a stoppage-time free kick by Marcel Sabitzer.

Additionally, a 2-0 victory over Hoffenheim between those defeats saw the hosts maintain their unbeaten streak on home turf this season, where they will hope to record a fourth win in five outings on Sunday.

Meanwhile, Merlin Polzin's Hamburger endured a dire start to the season, conceding 12 goals without reply in their first three Bundesliga games before firing back with a run of three consecutive triumphs.

It would be fair to say that HSV's term has been defined by streaks so far, alternating between trios of defeats and wins across all competitions, and the club will be hoping to stabilise after the international break.

Polzin's side were held to a 1-1 draw by Croatia's Hajduk Split in a friendly on November 15, following up a 3-1 success against Borussia Monchengladbach that helped to distance the team from the relegation zone in the German top flight.

That victory has left Hamburger 11th in the Bundesliga table with 12 points to their name - a total that puts them level with Eintracht Frankfurt, Hoffenheim and Stuttgart up to eighth - as well as five points clear of 16th-placed Union Berlin.

Earning another win on Sunday would be keeping with HSV's pattern this term, but after seeing the visitors lose four of their five away league matches in 2026-27, fans would be forgiven for harbouring doubts.

Werder Bremen form (all competitions):.

Hamburger SV form (all competitions):.

Werder will be without strikers Keke Topp (ACL) and Salim Musah (thigh) once again as they recover from long-term injuries, though the doubts about Marco Grull's fitness after he missed training with a calf issue will be a major concern for the team.

If Grull is sidelined on Sunday, then expect to see Niclas Fullkrug supported up top by Eren Dinkci, Chuki and Justin Njinmah.

Jens Stage and Skelly Alvero are also unavailable due to respective thigh and calf injuries, while question marks remain about the readiness of fellow midfielder Senne Lynen, who has been ill over the past week, though Youri Regeer and Ludovit Reis should be on hand to form Thioune's double pivot.

Elsewhere, the versatile Mitchell Weiser is a doubt with a thigh problem and left-back Moussa N'Diaye is recovering from a groin injury, so Arthur and Olivier Deman look set to start at full-back.

As for Hamburger, they are missing centre-back Jordan Torunarigha, who has been dealing with a hip matter, but Mario Vuskovic is likely to return after getting over a minor back injury.

The visitors are lighter in midfield than ideal, with all three of Albert Sambi Lokonga (calf), Bilal Nadir (thigh) and Nicolai Remberg (ACL) sidelined, so Martin Adeline could join Miro Muheim in the centre of the park, while Albert Gronbaek operates in the number 10 role.

Centre-forward Yussuf Poulsen is also out with a calf injury, but Terem Moffi and Patson Daka will be ready to lead the line in a strike partnership on Sunday.

Werder Bremen possible starting lineup:.

Hein; Arthur, Friedl, Pieper, Deman; Regeer, Reis; Dinkci, Chuki, Njinmah; Fullkrug.

Hamburger SV possible starting lineup:.

Heuer; Capaldo, Omari, Bornauw; El Ouahdi, Adeline, Muheim, Moller Wolfe; Gronbaek; Moffi, Daka.

Werder have been exceptional on home turf this season, and they will be expecting to collect all three points once again, but the match is likely to be closer than otherwise if Grull remains sidelined.

By contrast, Hamburger have struggled on the road throughout 2026-27, and with four defeats in five away Bundesliga games so far, expect to see the visitors' overall pattern of results broken.

Cole Palmer was involved in an angry exchange with Joao Pedro after the final whistle of Chelsea’s woeful home defeat to Leeds United.

Xabi Alonso’s side were thrashed 4-1 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon with the visitors scoring three times in the second-half to seal a famous win in the capital.

Emmanuel Emegha opened the scoring for the hosts after 25 minutes before Noah Okafor levelled the contest three minutes later.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin put Leeds back in front eight minutes into the second-half before Okafor added his second of the afternoon.

Brenden Aaronson wrapped things up with a fine solo effort in added time to seal win that moved Leeds ahead of Chelsea in the Premier League table.

Pedro was not in the squad, still recovering from a thigh injury that has now ruled him out of Chelsea’s last five games.

It had been hoped he would be fit after the international break but Xabi Alonso revealed on Friday the striker was still not back in training.

The Brazil international was in attendance on Saturday afternoon and was involved in a tense exchange with one of his teammates immediately after the game.

The Athletic report Palmer appeared to have an angry exchange of words with Pedro as he left the pitch.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

In footage shared on social media, Palmer is seen approaching his teammate, covering his mouth with his hand as he speaks. Pedro puts his arms on his teammate’s shoulders, shrugging his shoulders in response as Palmer walks away unhappy.

During Alonso’s post-match press conference, one journalist suggested the disagreement was sparked when Pedro tried to get Palmer to go and applaud the fans with the England international seemingly reluctant.

Alonso stated of the incident: ‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high and we feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I said, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still so long way to go..

Palmer had played the full 90 minutes but was unable to inspire his side who have now won just one of their last five games.

Published: 15:24 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 16:32 EST, 19 November 2026.

Blackpool have sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy birthday.

Industry observers note that evatt had been in charge for a year and his final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, when his squad was decimated by illness. The result left the Seasiders immediately above the League One relegation zone and followed a run of one win and six defeats in ten league games.

Blackpool’s social media team had earlier wished Evatt a happy 45th birthday with the pay-off line: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'.

Three hours later, Evatt was relieved of his duties, and the club began the search for their ninth manager in eight years.

Sources indicate that evatt’s contract was set to run until June 2028. He joined last October following his exit from Bolton Wanderers in January 2025.

Blackpool later thanked the 45-year-old for his efforts during his time with the club.

Blackpool sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy 45th birthday.

Blackpool posted the birthday message just after 9am in the morning, with Evatt's sacking then confirmed at 4pm.

Former Crystal Palace chairman Simon Jordan famously claimed to have sacked Trevor Francis on his birthday back in 2003.

Francis' dismissal has become an often told tale, with Jordan writing sixteen years after the event that he had even offered to send the former England star a birthday card.

Recent reports have also involved the suggestion that Francis had mumbled 'but its my birthday' back to Jordan when he was given his marching orders.

Industry observers note that whether these events played out as told are unclear. But Crystal Palace officially announced Francis' departure on April 18 in 2003, with his birthday falling a day later.

Sources indicate that 'I am totally committed to playing in the Premier League and I will ensure the new manager can achieve this aspiration,' Jordan wrote on Crystal Palace's website at the time. 'I would like to thank Trevor for all his hard work and would like to wish him the very best for the future.'.

Sources indicate that jordan then turned on the players, adding: 'I'm not watching next year what I've had to watch this year. At times we've been a disgrace.

'I've asked the management staff to tell me who should go. They can see the players who are performing and those who are not and you will see in the summer, out they will go. The players will be told when it suits me. I care about them as much they care about me.'.

Francis had reportedly told his players in a parting shot: 'Well, lads, I've been sacked – have a good summer holiday.'.

Palace appointed Steve Kember as manager in the summer and despite Jordan's hopes of automatic promotion, rather than the play-offs, found themselves in a relegation battle in November.

Iain Dowie was appointed as manager the following month and guided Palace into the play-offs, with the Eagles triumphing in Cardiff to secure promotion to the top flight.

Steve Thompson will step in to take charge of the team against Wigan Athletic this weekend, his fourth spell as caretaker, alongside Stephen Crainey, Stephen Dobbie and Steve Banks.

Industry observers note that during a hugely successful playing career at Bloomfield Road, Evatt made over 250 appearances for Blackpool. In his six years at the club, he played a vital role in their rise from League One to the Premier League, which included two successful play-off campaigns.

On arrival as a manager, he amassed 13 points from a possible 15 in December 2025 to lift them out of the relegation zone, although they lost ten and won two of their next 15 matches in all competitions.

They finished the campaign strongly, with six wins in seven games as part of a sequence of one defeat in 13 between mid-March and the end of August, only to struggle again this season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on fresh players really does take some doing.

Recent findings suggest that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

According to recent reports, A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

Sources indicate that for Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he noted. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

Recent findings suggest that indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

Sources indicate that spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

At the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi mentioned later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

“There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

Sources indicate that spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This new stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

It has been revealed that some surprised faces then when Moyes said later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”.

Recent findings suggest that the game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes said that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”.

In the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

Industry observers note that “I get where people are coming from. According to recent reports, “What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Sources indicate that alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Glenn Murray believes Bruno Fernandes will look to leave the club if he doesn’t sign a new Manchester United contract before the January transfer window.

Fernandes won the PFA Players’ Player of the Year last year after a superb second half of the season under Michael Carrick, but has not hit those same heights so far this campaign.

The Red Devils captain was also dropped for a game after publicly criticising Carrick’s tactics following a heavy Champions League defeat to Como.

The arrival of Mauricio Pochettino represents a fresh start for Fernandes this season, but there remains uncertainty over his long-term future at the club given the 32-year-old is out of contract at the end of the season.

Fernandes has already turned down two contract offers from the club, and former Brighton striker Murray believes he could be eyeing up a move away from Old Trafford when the transfer window reopens in January.

It has been revealed that ‘I wouldn’t burst the bank [on a new contract] for him,’ Murray told Sky Sports. ‘I think he’s not the future of the football club.

‘Listen, he’s given his best years to Manchester United and unfortunately they haven’t won an awful lot, which he would have liked.

‘I think if he gets the option to move on, and it gets to January, and he can start speaking to other people, I think it will open his eyes up to see where he could go and if he could win things and finish off his career more enjoyably, because there have been years at Manchester United that have been really difficult.

‘He has been the standout player, but he is not the future and it could be time to part ways.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It all depends on the salary because if you outlay a lot [on wages], there is nothing coming back on the other end at this point of his career.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pochettino, meanwhile, has confirmed that Fernandes will remain captain under his management and insisted the midfielder is an ‘important’ player for his rebuild.

‘All the players, we were chatting, it was amazing from day one, Bruno is our captain, an important player,’ Pochettino confirmed.

‘But all the players need to think they are crucial, from the bottom to the top.

‘I spent three hours, chatting in my office, with all the players, maybe I miss some injured players. In the next few days, we will talk in an individual way with all of them.

‘It’s vital to listen to what they need to say, understand the place they are. Not only on the field, off the field, what’s going on. Some conversations, some collective way, meetings, but focus is on Sunday.’.

AC Milan’s shirt sponsor Emirates are set to make a change ahead of the 2027-28 season, according to a report.

As per Footy Headlines, the ‘Fly Better’ text will be removed from the shirts of Arsenal, Real Madrid and Milan ahead of next season. Instead, the airline will simply display the word ‘Emirates’ across the middle of the clubs that they sponsor.

Sources indicate that as mentioned, it will not take effect immediately and will be something that is adopted from next season. The ‘Fly Better’ tagline started being seen in 2020 as a latest marketing slogan that replaced the iconic ‘Fly Emirates’.

The idea is to create a more ‘streamlined’ look on the kits, and that is also why we have been seeing leaked designs for next season that feature just the singular word.

Industry observers note that of course, this is not the only alteration from a kit perspective that Milan are gearing up for. In case you missed the big news of the past few weeks, Adidas are set to take over from PUMA ahead of 2028-29, for what will be a fourth stint as the manufacturer of the Rossoneri’s shirts.

Recent findings suggest that it is believed to be a record-breaking deal at least in Serie A, one that will net the club around €500m over the duration of the agreement. For many, it is a welcome return to a brand that became synonymous with Milan given the length of their last stint as the kit maker.

Today's Premier League predictions include Arsenal's trip to Newcastle United, and a contest between Manchester City and Fulham.

Seeking to end a three-game losing run in the Premier League, Manchester City welcome Fulham to the Etihad Stadium for Saturday’s lunchtime kickoff.

These two teams last butted heads nine months ago when three first-half goals helped the Citizens claim a comfortable 3-0 home victory.

Maresca will demand a strong reaction from his Man City players following recent setbacks, and their exceptional historical record in this fixture firmly establishes them as the favourites to claim all three points.

While a porous Citizens backline offers encouragement to a Fulham outfit that has drawn a blank in seven of their last 12 Premier League games on the road, we expect the hosts' attacking firepower to comfortably outgun the Cottagers on this occasion.

Industry observers note that > Click here to read our full preview for Man City vs. Fulham, including team news and predicted lineups.

Chelsea will be looking to return to winning ways and strengthen their top-four credentials when they take on Leeds United in Saturday afternoon’s Premier League contest at Stamford Bridge.

These two teams served up a nine-goal thriller in the EFL Cup just a couple of months ago, with the West Londoners securing a 6-3 comeback victory in the third round.

Chelsea have not been the same prolific outfit without the presence of Joao Pedro up front, and they could find it difficult to break down a robust Leeds backline without a natural focal point.

Despite only one of the Blues' last six Premier League matches seeing both teams score, we can see the net rippling at both ends on this occasion, with the hosts bouncing back from recent setbacks and edging to a slender victory.

> Click here to read our full preview for Chelsea vs. Leeds United, including team news and predicted lineups.

Sunderland will endeavour to claim back-to-back Premier League victories and climb out of the relegation zone when they travel to Villa Park to face Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon.

A seven-goal spectacular was witnessed when these two teams last locked horns in April, with Tammy Abraham netting a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 4-3 home triumph for Villa.

Aston Villa's game management has become a growing concern, and Sunderland should fancy their chances of finding the net given that the hosts have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their last six matches in all competitions.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Aston Villa took a "significant step forward" in their 0-0 draw with Sunderland, so says Unai Emery.

Villa drew a third straight Premier League match as they were frustrated by the Black Cats at Villa Park.

It is the first time Villa have drawn three straight Premier League games since 2014.

Villa attempted 700 passes in this match – their most on record (from 2003-04) in a single Premier League game, completing 624, their joint-most on record (also v Hull City in September this season).

They had 19 shots, but those chances were worth only 0.98 expected goals (xG) combined. Emery, though, was pleased with the levels demonstrated by his team on the occasion of his 150th Premier League game in charge of Villa.

Emery told Sky Sports: "A little bit frustrated, but how we are building our team and recovering our confidence in our style of playing, [this game] was a step forward.

"We were dominating, we were progressing with passes, and we were in a good position to control the game, but we didn't create many clear chances.

"But this is the way and the idea we have to try and implement. We avoided the moment of them dominating us and avoided giving up chances to the opponent. We did a lot of good things.

"It is not enough, but we know how we have to try and build the team and how we can feel better. One step forward, clear in the style. Keep going forward.".

Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland Not sure we'll remember this game, will we.

— Opta Analyst (@OptaAnalyst) November 21, 2026.

Sunderland, meanwhile, have picked up more points in their last four Premier League games (five – W1 D2 L1) than they had in their first seven this season beforehand (four – W1 D1 L5).

Regis Le Bris' team moved up into 18th, though they will slip back down to 19th should Manchester United avoid defeat at Liverpool on Sunday.

"Being hard to beat was one of the main objectives. It was really important to be solid, and I think the lads indicated a great mentality," Le Bris told BBC Sport.

"We had a few balls to exploit, and even at the end, with just a bit more maturity and more confidence, it was possible to score a goal.

"We showed we are a really good team when we want to defend together. I told them when you feel the opponents getting frustrated, it is a good sign, and it happened in the first half. A good point on the road.

According to recent reports, "The points are notable; sometimes you play well and don't get anything. It is the strength of the squad, the mindset and stability. I am really proud of that, as it is the foundation for the future.".

Crystal Palace defender Oscar Mingueza is a doubt for Thursday’s Europa League clash with Real Sociedad after missing out through injury against Coventry.

Mingueza was absent from the squad that travelled to Coventry for Thomas Frank’s first game in charge of Palace, and Standard Sport understands that the Spanish full-back has suffered an adductor overload.

The 27-year-old, who arrived at Palace on a free transfer over the summer, has been for a scan, and while his injury is not believed to be serious, it is unclear whether he will be fit to face Real Sociedad at Selhurst Park on Thursday evening.

Mingueza has played nine games in all competitions for Palace this season, but has started just twice in the Premier League, with fellow summer signing Anan Khalaili preferred on the right-hand side of defence.

Speaking about Mingueza’s injury before kick-off against Coventry, Frank said he was hopeful that he could be available against Sociedad.

Industry observers note that “Oscar Mingueza unfortunately picked up the smallest of knocks, keeping him out of this game. But we’re hopeful for Thursday,” Frank noted.

Palace tasted defeat in their first game under Frank as Dwight McNeil’s 85th-minute own-goal handed Coventry a 3-2 win at the CBS Arena.

They remain rooted to the bottom of the Premier League table, having won two of their opening 11 league games.

#72022. Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 90m • 📚 Deep Dive (17999 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 90 min read (17999 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~90 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation1.
  • Solid-organ cancers represent a complex spectrum of pathology, with the intricately associated TME having a pivotal role in disease progression and therapeutic response4,5.
  • Recent findings suggest that previous studies have identified distinct cell subpopulations within the TME based on their gene expression profiles, spatial distributions and functional characteristics17,18,19,20,21.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation1. Given the breadth and diversity of human tumour pathology and contributions of tumour microenvironment (TME) cells to disease progression, pan-cancer analysis is needed to bridge major themes of stromal and immune cell evolution. To date, however, efforts to compare the TME response across cancers have been limited in scope2,3. Here we conduct a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis by algorithmically screening thousands of publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets for stromal and immune signatures across species and tissue types. We demonstrate conserved hallmarks of host cell transcriptional programming in response to malignancy across 42 cancer types in more than 2,000 human and mouse tumour samples. These findings are codified as an interactive web atlas (tmeatlas.stanford.edu) and software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for the systematic interrogation of the TME in tumours.

Solid-organ cancers represent a complex spectrum of pathology, with the intricately associated TME having a pivotal role in disease progression and therapeutic response4,5. Within the TME, both stromal and immune cells have emerged as key modulators of tumour growth, invasion and metastasis1,6,7,8,9,10. However, different studies (often in single-organ contexts) have shown conflicting roles for these cells in promoting versus suppressing tumour growth11,12,13,14. The heterogeneity of the TME, both within individual tumours and across tumour types, poses a substantial challenge to understanding the functional diversity of tumour-associated stromal and immune cells3,15,16.

Recent findings suggest that previous studies have identified distinct cell subpopulations within the TME based on their gene expression profiles, spatial distributions and functional characteristics17,18,19,20,21. However, these findings stem largely from isolated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies22,23,24, and subsequent pan-cancer efforts have remained limited in size and scope3,25,26,27,28. To our knowledge, the largest cancer-associated fibroblast atlas to date integrates data from 1,116 samples across 10 tumour types29; the largest tumour endothelial cell atlas includes 575 samples across 19 tumour types30; and no specific tumour mural or nerve atlases have been generated. Pan-cancer immune cell atlases have been larger28, especially those focused on individual immune cell lineages31,32,33; however, these typically have not examined immune cell interactions within the broader TME.

In a recent development, here we integrated single-cell transcriptomic data from 3,381 human and mouse samples across 42 cancer types and 258 datasets to create a definitive TME transcriptional atlas. By mapping this massive cellular landscape, we resolved the stromal and immune ecosystem of solid tumours. Furthermore, by linking enriched subpopulations to poor clinical outcomes, we identified opportunities for future TME-targeted cancer therapies. Key computational predictions are subsequently validated through in vitro and in vivo experiments. Finally, we have consolidated this work into an interactive web atlas (tmeatlas.stanford.edu) and R software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for groups investigating the TME.

Industry observers note that to systematically analyse single-cell transcriptomic data, we evaluated every scRNA-seq cancer study published in the public domain between January 2014 and July 2025. Separate queries were evaluated independently for human and mouse datasets within the foundational public repositories for single-cell transcriptomics: the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and ArrayExpress. We screened a total of 3,975 published datasets (Fig. 1a). Studies specific to either blood or central nervous system cancers were excluded from our analysis, as were those failing to meet specific architectural requirements (Methods; see Fig. 1a,b). Our comprehensive screen identified 190 human and 68 mouse datasets (Supplementary Table 1), collectively comprising more than 15.4 million cells. Collectively, these datasets formed the final analytical cohort, comprising 3,381 individual scRNA-seq samples across 42 unique cancer types (Fig. 1b and Supplementary Tables 2 and 3).

Industry observers note that a, Systematic workflow detailing the scRNA-seq dataset curation process. The initial screen examined 3,975 datasets, of which 190 human and 68 mouse scRNA-seq remained after filtering. The combined 258 datasets comprised 3,381 samples and more than 15 million cells. Schematic created in BioRender; Wang, H. https://biorender.com/w8x4pii (2026). CNS, central nervous system. b, Illustration of all cancer types from human (top) and mouse (bottom) included in this study. HNSCC, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma; MPNST, malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour; NSCLC, non-small-cell lung cancer; SCLC, small-cell lung cancer. Illustration created in BioRender; Wang, H. https://biorender.com/p0byno1 (2026).

To process the more than 12.8 million human cells from 2,855 samples and 190 datasets (Extended Data Fig. 1a,b and Supplementary Fig. 1), nearly an order of magnitude greater than many recent seminal studies3,25,26,27,28,31,32,33,34, we used sketch-based sampling and memory read optimization (Extended Data Fig. 1c,d). We applied three independent approaches for data integration to reduce batch effects: Harmony, scVI and FastMNN (Extended Data Figs. 1e and 2a). We then projected each integrated result onto the full dataset (Extended Data Fig. 2b,c). Supervised annotation using four methods—canonical marker genes, estimated copy number variation (inferCNV), SingleR and scATOMIC (Extended Data Fig. 3 and Supplementary Fig. 2)—delineated the presence of seven main cell types across nearly all human cancers (Fig. 2a–c, Extended Data Fig. 1e,f and Supplementary Table 4). These encompass principal stromal (fibroblast, endothelial, mural and nerve) and immune (myeloid and lymphoid) lineages, alongside epithelial cells, which were excluded from subsequent characterization to focus on the two core TME compartments. Comparing the three integration approaches (Supplementary Table 5), Harmony demonstrated the most robust integration and was selected for all subsequent evaluations. The three integration approaches also frequently yielded discordant cell-type assignments for individual cells (Extended Data Fig. 2d–f), highlighting the stochasticity and misclassification risks inherent to relying on any single method35,36. To mitigate this, we provisionally pooled all cells assigned to a specific TME lineage by any of the three algorithms (Extended Data Fig. 1g). Misassigned cells within these overlapping pools were subsequently removed through recursive downstream filtering (Extended Data Fig. 1h and Supplementary Fig. 3a–e), generating final, high-fidelity atlases for the six principal TME cell types (Fig. 2d–i and Extended Data Fig. 1i,j).

a, UMAP embeddings of 12,855,771 cells from 190 human studies integrated using Harmony, with consensus seven cell-type annotations (outlined and labelled within the panel) derived through multiple annotation approaches (Extended Data Figs. 1 and 2 and Supplementary Figs. 1–3). Individual cells are labelled according to downstream final cell annotations in panels d–i. cDC, conventional dendritic cell; DC, dendritic cell; End, endothelial; Fib, fibroblast; Lym, lymphoid; Mac, macrophage; mem, memory; Mono, monocyte; mregDC, mature dendritic cell enriched in immunoregulatory molecules; Mur, mural; myel, myelinating; Myl, myeloid; Neut, neutrophil; NK, natural killer; SMC, smooth muscle cell; TFH, follicular helper T; Treg, regulatory T. b, Total number of human samples included for each type of cancer. c, Distribution of cell types for each cancer, after selecting for only unsorted samples. Abbreviations of cancer names are listed in Supplementary Table 2. d, UMAP embedding of CAFs, manually clustered into four parent populations (outlined and labelled within the UMAP) from a total of seven transcriptionally distinct subpopulations, the latter of which are coloured separately (top left). A dot plot displaying relative gene expression for characteristic markers of the seven transcriptionally distinct CAF subpopulations shown in the left panel (top right). Distributions of CAF subpopulations among tumour samples for different cancer types are also shown (bottom; n = 328,877 cells). e–i, UMAPs (top left), dot plots (top right) and distributions among tumour samples for different cancer types (bottom) for endothelial (e; n = 234,948 cells), mural (f; n = 162,178 cells), nerve (g; n = 7,655 cells), lymphoid (h; n = 1,580,785 cells) and myeloid (i; n = 805,111 cells) cells. Between 3 and 12 subpopulations are identified for each cell type, and one population-defining gene per subpopulation is displayed in the dot plot for each cell type (full list in Supplementary Tables 6 and 7).

We next characterized cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), the predominant stromal population in the TME37. Following our recursive isolation strategy (Extended Data Fig. 1h), we delineated four transcriptionally distinct CAF meta-clusters (Fig. 2d) expressing canonical markers (PDGFRA, LUM and DCN) and lacking non-fibroblast markers (Extended Data Fig. 4a and Supplementary Fig. 4). Specifically, we identified (1) antigen-presenting CAFs (apCAFs; class II HLA+), (2) immunomodulatory/inflammatory CAFs (iCAFs; cytokine+), (3) myofibroblastic/mechanoresponsive CAFs (mCAFs; extracellular matrix (ECM)+, mechanotransduction+), and (4) steady-state CAFs (ssCAFs; progenitor-like markers+; Fig. 2d), broadly consistent with observations from our previous work38 and that of others25,39,40,41. High-resolution sub-clustering (Fig. 2d, Supplementary Table 6 and 7 and Supplementary Fig. 4) further stratified these into seven subpopulations: two iCAF (CXCL8+ or ISG15+), two mCAF (LRRC15+ or COL4A1+), two ssCAF (PI16+ or CXCL14+) and one apCAF. All seven subpopulations were conserved across nearly all evaluated tumour types and tissues (Fig. 2d, bottom). Of note, apCAFs were nearly universally present, whereas previous studies had found them only in rare tumour subsets6. Furthermore, the human apCAFs that we identified did not express mesothelial markers such as MSLN, which are characteristic of mouse apCAFs42 (Extended Data Fig. 4a).

Recent findings suggest that comparing relative abundances between tumour and non-malignant tissues (Fig. 3a), both mCAF populations were significantly enriched in tumours (3.5-fold for LRRC15+; 2.7-fold for COL4A1+; Supplementary Table 8), reflecting cancer-induced desmoplasia37,43. Similarly, iCAFs and apCAFs were enriched in tumour samples (6.3-fold for ISG15+ iCAFs, 1.3-fold for CXCL8+ iCAFs and 2.0-fold for apCAFs), consistent with their roles in inducing immune evasion42 or secreting inflammatory cytokines41. Analysing abundance across tumour stage and patient treatment response, we found ISG15+ iCAFs, LRRC15+ mCAFs and COL4A1+ mCAFs significantly enriched in late-stage (III–IV) versus early-stage (I–II) tumours (1.9-fold, 1.3-fold and 1.2-fold, respectively; Fig. 3b). Treatment responsiveness did not significantly correlate with any CAF subpopulation (Fig. 3c). Overall, ISG15+ iCAFs were the most consistently enriched fibroblast subset defining both the malignant state and advanced disease (Fig. 3a–c, blue box).

a–c, Forest plots of cell subpopulation proportions, relative to their parent population, between tumour and non-malignant samples (a), advanced-stage (3–4) versus early-stage (1–2) cancer (b), and treatment non-responders versus responders (c). The blue box in panel a highlights ISG15+ iCAFs. Non-malignant samples comprise tissue resected adjacent to a tumour, pooled with tissue from individuals or animals without tumours. The points show fold enrichment, the ratio of weighted mean per-sample proportions; the unit of replication is the individual scRNA-seq sample, weighted by the square root of its cell number. The error bars show the propagated standard error of that ratio (see Methods). Significance was determined by two-sided weighted Welch t-tests, with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment within each parent lineage; the colour denotes adjusted P < 0.05. All samples are biologically independent; n = 859–1,777 (a), 311–658 (b) and 48–108 (c) samples per parent lineage. Exact n, group means, standard errors, fold enrichments with 95% confidence intervals, test statistics and exact P values are provided in Supplementary Table 8. d, Immunofluorescence for apCAFs (PDGFRα+HLA-DR+ co-staining) in tumour and matched tumour-adjacent tissue from PDAC, CRC and PTC. The white boxes mark co-staining. n = 7 PDAC, 3 CRC and 3 PTC biologically independent specimens; each was stained and imaged once, with comparable patterns within each tumour type. Scale bars, 100 µm. e, Pseudotemporal manifold from a published PDAC dataset62, with yellow indicating ECM regions of high pseudotime and blue showing low pseudotime (left). UMAP is coloured by overall survival; higher pseudotime accompanies shorter survival (right). f, PDAC tissue microarray with haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining (left) and ECM pseudotime (right); the blue and yellow boxes mark the low-pseudotime and high-pseudotime regions shown in panels g,h. Scale bar, 200 µm. g,h, Histology and CODEX of those regions with low matrix pseudotime and good patient survival (g) and high matrix pseudotime and poor patient survival (h). H&E (top left); remaining panels, CODEX for the indicated markers. The white boxes mark putative apCAFs: HLA-DR+ spindle-like cells in areas of high COL1A1/αSMA expression without tumour or other immune markers. CODEX was performed on n = 3 biologically independent PDAC specimens, each analysed once in a single multiplexed run. Scale bars, 50 µm.

Sources indicate that focusing on the iCAF compartment, our atlas revealed two distinct and conserved transcriptional states: ISG15+ iCAFs exhibiting canonical interferon-γ (IFNγ) stimulation (for example, CXCL10)44, and CXCL8+ iCAFs expressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (for example, CXCL1)41. Crucially, these iCAF subpopulations provide additional granularity compared with previously reported CXCL12+ iCAFs39. Recent consensus frameworks have identified CXCL12 to be among the steady-state fibroblast hallmark genes rather than specific to a malignancy-induced inflammatory CAF state25. In line with this, our CXCL14+ ssCAFs co-expressed high levels of CXCL12 while maintaining a homeostatic signature. Abundance analyses revealed divergent ssCAF dynamics: conventional PI16+ ssCAFs (which also strongly express CXCL12) were heavily enriched in non-malignant tissue (2.8-fold), potentially representing a progenitor pool, whereas the CXCL14+ pool remained proportionally stable across benign and malignant tissues (1.0-fold), typifying embedded parenchymal fibroblasts. We therefore propose that traditional ‘CXCL12+ iCAFs’ are more accurately classified as tissue-resident CXCL14+ ssCAFs.

In a recent development, to elucidate the regulatory networks driving these distinct states, we examined transcription factor activity using SCENIC. The apCAF population exhibited elevated inferred activity of RUNX3 and IKZF1, regulators of MHC class II expression45, suggesting a mechanism for direct T cell interaction and immunotherapy resistance (Extended Data Fig. 5a). The ISG15+ iCAFs showed predicted activation of ETV7 and IRF2, implicating suppressive cytokine signalling in tumour progression46 (Extended Data Fig. 5b). Both mCAF populations were enriched for CREB3L1 and NKX3-2, linked to ECM overexpression and stiffness (Extended Data Fig. 5c). Conversely, ssCAF populations exhibited higher predicted activity of CEBPA and FOXO3, which regulate lineage and redox homeostasis, respectively, consistent with the homeostatic properties ascribed to this population26 (Extended Data Fig. 5d). Overall, these regulatory profiles broadly align with the putative functional roles attributed to each CAF subpopulation.

Industry observers note that to evaluate whether specific populations could be distinguished by differences in metabolic programs, we applied scMetabolism to analyse our scRNA-seq dataset. Of note, we observed that LRRC15+ mCAFs were enriched for genes associated with elevated oxidative phosphorylation, in contrast to the traditional glycolytic programs of ISG15+ iCAFs (Extended Data Fig. 5e,f and Supplementary Fig. 5a–c). These profiles align with the distinct energy demands of each cell type: iCAFs expressed genes linked with rapid glycolytic ATP generation that would permit overproduction of pro-inflammatory cytokines, whereas mCAFs were predicted to utilize the more efficient oxidative phosphorylation, enabling them to sustain intense ECM production and remodelling driving the desmoplastic response to neoplasia47. ssCAFs exhibited globally lower expression of metabolic pathway genes, reinforcing their relatively quiescent state.

Industry observers note that to determine whether these distinct functional and metabolic states ultimately impact patient survival, we paired bulk RNA-seq and clinical outcome data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) using CIBERSORTx deconvolution (Supplementary Table 9 and Supplementary Fig. 6a,b). Patients whose tumours were estimated to have higher abundances of apCAFs, iCAFs or mCAFs exhibited worse overall survival across most cancer types, consistent with previous observations48. By contrast, we observed a positive (but not statistically significant; 1.3-fold, P = 0.27) relationship between CXCL14+ ssCAF proportion and patient survival. Together, these results suggest that fibroblast differentiation and lineage progression may be associated with worse outcomes in solid-organ tumours, reflecting a pro-tumorigenic role for apCAFs, iCAFs and mCAFs.

Industry observers note that beyond fibroblasts, we examined tumour endothelial, mural and nerve cells, which drive angiogenesis, cytokine signalling and metastatic spread1,7,8,49. In silico isolation of endothelial cells (Extended Data Fig. 1a–j) identified five pan-cancer subpopulations (Fig. 2e): GJA5+ arterial, CA4+ capillary, PROX1+ lymphatic, ESM1+ tip and ACKR1+ venous. All expressed canonical markers (PECAM1, VWF and CDH5) and lacked non-endothelial signatures (Extended Data Fig. 4b, Supplementary Table 6 and Supplementary Fig. 7). Of note, angiogenic ESM1+ tip cells50 were the sole endothelial subpopulation significantly enriched in tumours versus non-malignant tissue (1.7-fold; Fig. 3a and Supplementary Table 8), reflecting dysfunctional tumour neovascularization51. These tip cells, co-expressing FLT1 (VEGFR1) and KDR (VEGFR2), were significantly elevated in treatment non-responsive tumours (1.9-fold; Fig. 3c). Furthermore, they correlated with elevated metabolic activity (Extended Data Fig. 5g and Supplementary Fig. 5d) and worse overall survival across most TCGA cohorts (Supplementary Fig. 6b). These data reinforce the pro-tumorigenic role of tip cells7,52,53, which may continuously support growth by rapidly initiating marginal angiogenesis, highlighting them as candidate targets for multi-drug therapy.

Subclustering of pan-cancer mural cells delineated six distinct subpopulations (Fig. 2f): CCL2+, CD248+ and ISG15+ pericytes; RERGL+ and WFDC1+ vascular smooth muscle cells; and DES+ visceral smooth muscle cells. All expressed canonical markers (RGS5, PDGFRB and CSPG4) and lacked non-mural signatures (Supplementary Table 6 and Supplementary Fig. 8). ISG15+ and CD248+ pericytes, alongside WFDC1+ vascular smooth muscle cells, were significantly enriched in tumours versus non-malignant tissue (4.5-fold, 1.8-fold and 1.2-fold, respectively; Fig. 3a and Supplementary Table 8), with ISG15+ pericytes also exhibiting elevated overall metabolic activity (Extended Data Fig. 5h). Clinically, CD248+ pericytes correlated with poor treatment response (1.8-fold; Fig. 3c). Mechanistically, both tumour-enriched pericyte populations expressed ECM genes (COL1A1, COL3A1 and COL4A1), supporting a role in tumour desmoplasia (Supplementary Fig. 5e,f). Of note, PIEZO2, which encodes a mechanotransduction channel, was detected in a small subset of CD248+ pericytes and was not detected in other mural populations (Supplementary Fig. 8). Detection was sparse and expression levels were low, indicating selective rather than robust population-specific expression. Given the established role of PIEZO2 in cellular mechanosensation54, we hypothesize that this fraction of pro-fibrotic pericytes may be activated by the stiffened TME to further upregulate ECM production, a possibility that merits further investigation.

In a recent development, finally, we analysed tumour-associated nerve cells, filtering out neural crest cancers to avoid transcriptional overlap with nerve-based tumours49. Our analysis revealed three distinct subpopulations and their canonical markers: MLANA+ melanocytes, MPZ+ myelinating Schwann cells and NGFR+ non-myelinating Schwann cells (Fig. 2g, Supplementary Table 6 and Supplementary Fig. 9). Subpopulation proportions varied markedly across tumour types (Fig. 2g, bottom). Because this heterogeneity probably reflects both tissue-specific neural architecture and the general rarity of nerve cells in standard biopsies, these populations were omitted from subsequent downstream analyses.

In a recent development, comprising over 2.4 million cells, immune cells constituted the largest TME compartment in our atlas. In silico isolation broadly segregated these into lymphoid and myeloid lineages. Focusing first on lymphoid cells—primary mediators of antitumour immunity55—we identified 11 subpopulations: CD4+ (3) and CD8+ (3) T cells, natural killer cells (1), B cells (3) and plasma cells (1; Fig. 2h, Supplementary Table 6 and Supplementary Fig. 10). Nearly all T cell populations were significantly enriched in tumours (Fig. 3a). This was driven primarily by CD8+ISG15+ IFN-primed T cells (2.4-fold) and CD8+GZMB+ tumour-reactive exhausted T (TEX) cells (1.5-fold). Of note, this GZMB+ population was also significantly enriched in early-stage disease (Fig. 3b), reflecting an initial wave of localized antitumour immunity undergoing rapid, chronic antigen-driven dysfunction56. In addition, FOXP3+ regulatory T cells (1.8-fold) and CXCL13+ follicular helper T cells (1.6-fold) were both enriched in tumours. By contrast, B cell and plasma populations were comparatively depleted within the tumour but enriched in non-malignant tissue, probably reflecting peritumoural accumulation and immune exclusion from the tumour core57.

According to recent reports, examining tumour myeloid cells, we identified dendritic cells (three populations), monocytes (two populations), macrophages (four populations), mast cells, neutrophils and osteoclasts (Fig. 2i, Supplementary Table 6 and Supplementary Fig. 11). Most spanned all tumour types, except the tissue-specific osteoclasts (Fig. 2i, bottom). Three macrophage subtypes and LAMP3+ mature immunoregulatory dendritic cells were significantly tumour enriched (Fig. 3a), with SPP1+ and MARCO+ subpopulations further enriched in late-stage disease (Fig. 3b). SPP1+ macrophages (GPNMB+ and APOC1+) are known drivers of desmoplasia and poor clinical outcomes32, whereas late-stage MARCO+ enrichment suggests a specialized role in immunosuppression and hindered phagocytosis. Conversely, C1QC+ macrophages maintain a homeostatic, complement-rich signature (C1QA–C and FOLR2) linked to T cell infiltration and a non-exhausted TME58. LAMP3+ mature immunoregulatory dendritic cells (IDO1+ and CCR7+) represent a critical regulatory checkpoint, limiting cytotoxic T cell activity to facilitate late-stage immune evasion59. Finally, shared ISG15+ ‘IFN-primed’ clusters across both macrophages and T cells suggest a common axis of chronic inflammation driving terminal exhaustion via sustained type I IFN signalling31,32.

According to recent reports, to evaluate alignment with broader transcriptional consensus models, we performed quantitative cell-level comparisons against four pan-cancer reference atlases using pairwise expression mapping via our scTME software package60 (Extended Data Fig. 6a–d). Most of our subpopulations exhibited strong, reciprocal alignment with comparable cell types across datasets (for example, PI16+ ssCAFs, LRRC15+ mCAFs, ESM1+ tip cells, C1QC+/SPP1+ macrophages and FOXP3+ regulatory T cells). These comparisons also differentiated several of our newly characterized and finely partitioned subpopulations. The IFN-primed (ISG15+) axis mapped robustly to analogous IFN-activated states across lineages (Extended Data Fig. 6b). In addition, our newly identified ISG15+ pericytes mapped to parent pericytes (Extended Data Fig. 6a) but diverged from CD248+ pericytes in broader TME atlases by lacking myofibroblast overlap, reinforcing their distinct state (Extended Data Fig. 6c,d). Furthermore, CXCL14+ fibroblasts mapped predominantly to non-inflammatory populations—unlike the CXCL8+ and ISG15+ iCAF subpopulations—supporting their separation from canonical iCAFs. Overall, although our TME atlas is broadly congruent with established datasets, our fibroblast and mural subpopulations reflect a uniquely refined, data-driven partitioning with functional relevance.

In a recent development, our meta-analysis identified apCAFs across nearly all evaluated tumour types (Fig. 2d, bottom), far exceeding the limited number of cancers in which they have been validated in vivo6. Therefore, we performed immunohistochemistry to confirm their presence in previously uncharacterized tumour types. Co-staining for the membranous fibroblast marker PDGFRα and the antigen-presenting marker HLA-DR confirmed apCAF presence in human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) controls61, as well as in previously non-validated colorectal cancer (CRC) and papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) tissues, as predicted by our atlas (Fig. 3d). To exclude possible immune cell misclassification, we analysed multiplexed spatial proteomic (CODEX) data from human PDAC62. Spindle-like HLA-DR+ cells localized to highly fibrotic (COL1A1+/αSMA+) regions, lacked immune or epithelial markers (Fig. 3g,h), and occupied distinct ECM architectures associated with poor patient outcomes (Fig. 3e,f and Supplementary Fig. 12a–f). We further orthogonally validated apCAF presence using public Xenium spatial transcriptomic datasets63,64 (Supplementary Fig. 13a–c). scRNA-seq revealed only a modest correlation between apCAF and T cell abundances in tumour samples (Supplementary Fig. 14a), suggesting that apCAF expansion occurs regional to but independent of direct T cell support. By contrast, ISG15+ iCAFs strongly correlated with CD8+ISG15+ IFN-primed T cells (Supplementary Fig. 14b), supporting our hypothesis that this CAF population interacts with T cells to drive exhaustion and promote immune evasion.

To infer interaction networks, we paired CellChat receptor–ligand predictions with orthogonal NicheNet modelling of downstream transcriptional targets. Because multiple lineages harboured ISG15+ clusters, we first evaluated the IFNγ network. CellChat predicted robust signalling from CD8+GZMB+ tumour-reactive TEX cells to ISG15+ iCAFs (Fig. 4a), which was corroborated by NicheNet (Fig. 4b). These aligned predictions support the hypothesis that ISG15+ iCAFs act as direct responders to chronic, T cell-derived IFNγ within the TME. Applying this approach to explore drivers of dysfunctional neovascularization, CellChat predicted that ESM1+ endothelial tip cells receive disproportionately high VEGF signalling from tumour-associated macrophages and monocytes (Extended Data Fig. 7a). NicheNet further corroborated this relationship (Extended Data Fig. 7b), successfully recapitulating this established myeloid-driven angiogenic axis using data solely from our atlas65. Conversely, NicheNet did not directly substantiate several other CellChat-predicted receptor–ligand pairings as transcriptional drivers, suggesting that these specific interactions may operate via indirect or non-transcriptional mechanisms (Extended Data Fig. 7c,d and Supplementary Fig. 15a–d).

The blue arrows highlight interactions of interest. b, NicheNet heatmap of regulatory potential for T CD8+GZMB+ to ISG15+ iCAF signalling displays prioritized sender ligands on the y axis and their regulatory potential against predicted target genes on the x axis. c, Schematic illustrating the strategy for in vitro experiments in panels d–h.
